title: Chapter 17: Fu An Apartments
html:
To an outsider, Wang Qi’s insistence that a newcomer leave might itself have seemed suspicious. Chen Ge therefore made no promises. In fact, after hearing the man’s story, he suspected Wang Qi was still hiding something.

“I’ve told you everything I know, and there’s still time to leave. Once the clock strikes twelve, this building becomes something else.” With that, Wang Qi brushed the dust from his clothes and walked away.

Only after Wang Qi’s shadow disappeared into the darkness did Chen Ge snap out of his thoughts. He had approached the man hoping for answers about the building; instead, he had ended up with even more questions.

He’s certainly strange, but I can’t tell whether he’s unstable, lying, or telling the truth.Remembering Wang Qi’s unfocused eyes, Chen Ge felt uneasy. The exhaustion and pain in the man’s expression had seemed completely genuine. Whatever else is true, he really does seem to love his fiancée.

On his way back upstairs, Chen Ge paused outside the woman’s room on the first floor. After a moment of hesitation, he knocked.

“Hey, fresh blood!” The woman’s door remained closed, but to Chen Ge’s surprise, the door directly opposite swung open. A lanky man in his thirties leaned against the frame. He was badly groomed, with a beard that nearly blended into his hair, and a peony tattoo covered the back of one hand.

“And you are?” Chen Ge turned, instantly alert.

“The man handing out those missing-person notices isn’t even a tenant here, and his story doesn’t add up. Don’t believe everything he tells you, and try not to get too close to him.”

This was Chen Ge’s first time seeing the lanky man. Despite his rough appearance, his behavior seemed more ordinary than anyone else Chen Ge had met in the building. “Wang Qi does act strangely, but maybe losing his fiancée pushed him into it.”

“Did he tell you his fiancé disappeared around this apartment?”

“Yes.”

“Did he tell you the police gave him that information and that’s why he’s been searching for her here?”

“Yes.”

The man gave a humorless chuckle. “I’ve lived here for nine months, and I’ve never once seen the police come around. That man is lying to you. You don’t actually believe his ghost stories, do you?”

He leaned against the doorway. “There are no ghosts in this world. At most, there are people pretending to be ghosts. Anyway, it’s getting late. You should go back to your room.”

Chen Ge thanked him and headed upstairs. As he climbed, he thought, One of them is obviously lying. The question is which one.

Lost in thought, Chen Ge did not realize he had climbed all the way to the third floor. A faded number was painted in the corner of the wall, while the motion-activated light overhead flickered unsteadily. The entire floor had been left in disrepair. Grime coated the floor, scorch marks stained the corridor, and the wall covering peeled away in strips, revealing deep, dark gouges beneath.

Why did they leave the third floor like this? Was there no money for repairs, or is there another reason?

The motion-activated light went out, plunging Chen Ge into darkness. His work at the Haunted House had made him comfortable in unlit spaces, so the sudden darkness did not rattle him. He reached for his phone, but before he could turn on the flashlight, a shadow darted across the corridor.

“Who’s there?!” His phone flashlight swept across the third floor, but the shadow was gone. Chen Ge was about to investigate when he heard footsteps coming up the stairs.

It’s the landlord?If the short-tempered landlord caught him wandering around the forbidden third floor, he might throw him out. After a moment’s thought, Chen Ge pocketed his phone and quietly retreated to the second floor.

As he rounded the stairwell corner, Chen Ge saw a short, heavyset man emerge from a second-floor room carrying a basin. The man had been humming cheerfully, but the moment he noticed Chen Ge, his expression changed and he hurried away.

What was that about? Do I really look that frightening?Back in his room, Chen Ge lay on the bed with his backpack hugged against his chest. It feels like there isn’t a single normal person in this building. Any one of them could be connected to the murders.

The thought made Chen Ge sit bolt upright in bed.Wait. The mission told me to find whoever was responsible for the murders—it never said there was only one person. If there were multiple victims, there could have been multiple perpetrators as well. I need to learn more about what happened here years ago.

Chen Ge pulled out his phone. His conversation with Wang Qi had not been a complete waste; he had learned one important fact. Before it became Ping An Apartments, the building had been called Fu An Apartments.

He searched for “Jiujiang Fu An Apartments.” A few pages into the results, a string of chilling headlines appeared.

“Family of Four Killed at Fu An Apartments; Suspect Still Missing.”

“Accident or Arson? Questions Remain After Fu An Apartments Fire.”

“Old Case Reopened as New Evidence Emerges.”

As Chen Ge read through the old reports, a chill crept over him. This was not some made-up horror story. Real people had died here, and he was spending the night in the same building.

Five years earlier, a neighbor had noticed smoke rising from Fu An Apartments and called the fire department. The blaze was brought under control, but the investigation that followed quickly raised questions.

At first, investigators believed it had been an accident. As they examined the building, however, several details suggested otherwise.

The damage was inconsistent with a single accidental outbreak, and investigators found signs that the fire had spread from more than one area.

Those findings shifted the investigation toward suspected arson.

Police later confirmed that four members of the family who ran the apartments had died in the fire.

The case drew considerable attention, but much of the evidence had been destroyed. Despite an extensive investigation, the police were unable to identify or locate the person responsible.

The building remained sealed for a year. Afterward, ownership passed to the former owner’s father, and Fu An Apartments was renamed Ping An Apartments.

An entire family died here, and whoever caused it was never caught. No wonder people say this place is haunted.Strangely, learning the history made Chen Ge feel a little steadier. At least now he had some idea what he was dealing with.

Then one detail in the reports caught his attention.The articles say the owner was forty-one when he died. The property later passed to his father, so the current legal owner should be in his sixties or seventies by now.
